page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6455B processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache allocation consists of 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 60 MB L3 cache. Advanced instruction set support includes AVX-512 extensions and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8) matrix multiplication acceleration. System memory provides 64.0 GB of high-frequency 5 GHz DDR5 RAM, achieving an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance operates without bundled local storage and includes a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight elevated single-thread capability driven by the 3.9 GHz core frequency. In synthetic testing, the instance scored 2226.0 in single-core Geekbench and 2903.0 in text processing, both placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded data compression throughput reached 34.55 GB/sec in gzip and 14.85 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, outperforming 75% of peer instances. Multi-threaded metrics align with the 8-vCPU allocation, producing 8490.0 on Geekbench multi-core, 8648.24 on multi-core stress-ng, and 10.89 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. Memory throughput reached 70.75 GB/sec on large uncached read operations and 57.95 GB/sec on writes.

Because the r7iz.2xlarge combines high DDR5 memory density with high sustained clock rates, it offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for applications that incur per-core licensing fees while demanding large memory buffers. Tradeoffs include modest baseline network speeds of 3 Gbps and complete reliance on remote block storage, as no local NVMe drives are provisioned. This hardware profile aligns with memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, enterprise text processing, and single-thread-sensitive financial simulations.
